sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 24.2% a year from $1.70 billion in FY2016 to $12.0 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The FY2020 step change, revenue up 49.1% to $6.21 billion, came from the U.S. launch of TRIKAFTA in the fourth quarter of 2019 and KAFTRIO in the EU in the third quarter of 2020 [F5][D194][P51].
FY2024 broke the trend with a $233 million operating loss, driven by $4.4 billion of non-deductible acquired in-process R&D from the Alpine acquisition [F24][P5][P11].
FY2025 recovered to $4.17 billion of operating income, but revenue growth slowed to 8.9% as TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO grew only 0.7% [F25][D446][D530].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO supplied 85.9% of FY2025 revenue and contributed just 0.7pp of the 8.9% growth [D529][D531][D446].
ALYFTREK, launched in FY2025, added 7.6pp of growth on $838 million of sales, or 7.0% of revenue [D590][S69][D589].
Net product revenues rose $950.5 million, or 9%, in FY2025 on continued demand, per the filing [P3][S39].
Operating costs fell 30.4% while revenue grew 8.9%, so incremental operating margin reached 449.1% [D457][D446][D463].
Diluted EPS rose to $15.32 from $13.89 while the diluted share count was flat at 258.0 million [F75][F73][X137][D459].
FY2025 operating margin of 34.8% sits above the 31.8% window median but below the 48.2% FY2022 high [F35][D663][D662].
The 36.9pp margin recovery was mostly a 37.7pp swing in other lines as the FY2024 acquired IPR&D charge did not repeat [D452][D468].
Cost of revenue held at 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 on a lower overall royalty rate for the CF medicines [D425][P4].
SG&A rose 19.7%, cutting margin 1.3pp, while R&D grew 7.7% and added 0.4pp [D456][D467][D455][D466].
The FY2024 effective tax rate of 315.5% reflected the non-deductible Alpine IPR&D; FY2025 normalized to 14.9% [D390][D433][P5].
Operating cash flow of $3.63 billion in FY2025 came primarily from $4.17 billion of income from operations [F85][F25][P1].
Free cash flow of $3.19 billion was 0.81x net income, below the 1.07x window median and the 1.11x peer median [F105][F45][D435][D675][D694].
Capex rose 47.0% to $438 million, 3.6% of revenue and 2.09x D&A [F95][D447][D430][D436].
Days inventory outstanding climbed to 373 days from 287, the working-capital drag on conversion [D444][D397].
Cash and investments of $12.3 billion against no debt give net cash of 102.7% of revenue, the 88th percentile of eight biopharma peers [D438][D439][D440][D691].
Cash rose 9.8% in FY2025 primarily on increased cash and marketable securities from product revenue [D460][P2].
Buybacks of $2.02 billion absorbed 63.2% of free cash flow, yet the diluted share count was unchanged [D441][D442][D459].
Return on average equity of 22.5% trails the 38.7% peer median [D445][D696].
Days inventory outstanding rose 85 days to 373 in FY2025, a second straight large increase from 214 in FY2023 [D444][D397][D350].
Inventory is growing far faster than revenue, which ties up cash and risks write-downs if demand shifts [D462][D446].
The FY2025 tax rate fell 300.7pp from the distorted FY2024 level, a base effect rather than a new concern [D433][D390][R2].
FY2019 buybacks were later restated to $186.0 million from $192.0 million; the pack uses the first-reported figure [X141][R3].
If TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO growth stays near the FY2025 0.7% and ALYFTREK does not repeat its 7.6pp contribution, total growth would fall below the 8.9% level [D530][D590][D446].
A further rise in days inventory outstanding above 373 days would confirm the working-capital drag on the 0.81x cash conversion [D444][D435].
Operating margin holding above the 31.8% window median in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the FY2025 recovery [D663][F35].
